entries.label: Rigged!: Who governs the US?
entries.summary: US institutions are tested in unprecedented ways around the 2020 election.
entries.quote: We've never listed US domestic politics as our Top Risk, but in 2020, US institutions will be tested in unprecedented ways.

entries.label: The Great Decoupling
entries.quote: The decision by China and the US to decouple in the technology sphere is the single most impactful geopolitical development for globalization since the Soviet Union collapsed.

entries.label: US/China
entries.summary: Diverging political systems bring an open clash over security, influence and values.
entries.quote: Divergences between the US and China's political structures are bringing irreconcilable differences to the fore, and tensions will lead to a more explicit clash over national security, influence, and values.

entries.label: MNCs not to the rescue
entries.summary: Stronger states give multinationals a more confrontational environment.
entries.quote: Nation-states are reasserting themselves, presenting corporates with a significantly more confrontational regulatory and geopolitical environment going forward.

entries.label: India gets Modi-fied
entries.summary: Modi's focus on divisive social policy over economic reform has costs in 2020.
entries.quote: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has spent much of his second term promoting controversial social policies at the expense of an economic agenda. The impacts will be felt in 2020.

entries.label: Geopolitical Europe
entries.summary: Europe starts to push back against Washington and Beijing.
entries.quote: For years, Europe has proven unable or unwilling to effectively push back where it disagreed with Washington or, increasingly, Beijing. This is about to change.

entries.label: Politics vs. economics of climate change
entries.summary: Companies must choose between emission pledges and profits.
entries.quote: Climate change will create a collision course for corporate decision-makers, who must choose between commitments to reduce emissions and bottom lines.

entries.label: Shia crescendo
entries.summary: Failing US policy toward Shia-led states threatens regional stability.
entries.quote: US policy toward the major Shia-led nations in the Middle East is failing. That creates significant risks for regional stability.

entries.label: Discontent in Latin America
entries.summary: Public anger keeps political instability risk high across Latin America.
entries.quote: Public anger over sluggish growth, corruption, and low-quality public services will keep the risk of political instability high across Latin America in 2020.

entries.label: Turkey
entries.quote: President Recep Tayyip Erdogan has entered a period of steep political decline. With a long history of provocative behavior in response to threats, his weakness will lead him to lash out.

entries.label: The new axis of evil
entries.summary: Eurasia Group does not expect confrontations with Iran, North Korea or Venezuela to blow up.
entries.quote: The new “axis of evil" is unlikely to blow up, despite the headlines.
entries.note: Red herrings are not ranked; rank is the printed order.

entries.label: Populist policies in the developed world
entries.summary: Eurasia Group expects advanced democracies to withstand populism in 2020.
entries.quote: The world's advanced industrial democracies remain well-positioned to withstand the populist storm in 2020.
entries.note: Red herrings are not ranked; rank is the printed order.

entries.label: Post-Brexit
entries.summary: Eurasia Group expects little Brexit impact in 2020 after the UK election.
entries.quote: A big win for Boris Johnson gives Britain a much-needed break from Brexit madness.
entries.note: Red herrings are not ranked; rank is the printed order.
